title: Lytica POC scoping - open models
summary: AE + SE from Redwood scoped a 6-week POC with Lytica to validate open-model options for a multilingual customer support summarization workflow. Discussed success criteria (quality thresholds, latency SLOs, cost targets), workload sizing (concurrency, tokens per request), benchmark plan, and a short open-model shortlist. Agreed next steps and action items for both sides.
action_items: Jordan Hayes: send POC proposal and pricing (due: 2026-05-04)
Priya Nair: share benchmark template and previous open-model results (due: 2026-05-02)
Samir Patel: provide representative request samples and traffic profile (due: 2026-05-03)
Leo Ruiz: share security requirements and SOC2/ISO checklist (due: 2026-05-05)
next_steps: Jordan to send POC SOW and pricing by 2026-05-04
Customer to upload 500 representative transcripts + labels and traffic profile by 2026-05-03
Schedule baseline benchmark (1 week) once data received
Security sync between Leo and Redwood security team to confirm encryption/KMS and VPC options
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-30
Time: 14:00 - 14:42 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Ava Martinez (Head of ML, Lytica), Samir Patel (Platform Eng, Lytica), Maya Chen (Product, Lytica), Leo Ruiz (Security, Lytica)

[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Jordan from Redwood, AE for this region. Priya from our SE team is here as well. How's everyone doing?
[00:05] Ava (Lytica): Good, thanks. Excited to chat - we've been evaluating open models for a POC around multilang support for our support summarization pipeline.
[00:12] Priya (Redwood): Great. Agenda - quick intros, goals & success criteria, workload sizing, model shortlist and quality tradeoffs, benchmark plan and timelines, security/Q&A, then next steps. Any additions?
[00:22] Samir: That sounds right. We'll probably spend time on throughput - we have bursty traffic.
[00:28] Jordan: Perfect. Quick intros - Priya you want to say hi?
[00:30] Priya: Sure. I'm Priya, SE focused on inference performance and benchmarks - latency, batching, quant. I'll lead the bench plan.
[00:36] Maya: I'm Maya on product - responsible for evaluation criteria and success metrics.
[00:40] Leo: Leo, security. I'll own the compliance asks.
[00:44] Jordan: Cool. First, what does success look like for Lytica's POC? Ava?
[00:48] Ava: High level - we want to prove we can replace our current fine-tuned hosted model with an open model plus retrieval + lightweight fine-tune. Success metrics: human-rated summary quality >= baseline on our eval (we use a 5-point scale), automatic similarity metrics - e.g., ROUGE/LUKE-ish - show parity within 5%, latency p95 under 700ms for single-turn summarization, and cost target around 30-40% less per 1k tokens compared to our current provider. Also must pass security checks (no PD exfiltration, VPC option).
[01:15] Jordan: Good concrete targets. Priya, on workload sizing what did they share?
[01:18] Priya: Samir, can you outline traffic?
[01:20] Samir: Sure. Avg requests/day ~120k, peaks to 600 req/min during US morning, average tokens per request ~600 tokens (input+output), concurrency ~50 during peaks. We have some long dialogs too up to 2k tokens but rare. We plan to run retrieval offline so most calls are inference-only with a small retrieval call.
[01:38] Priya: That helps. For the POC we'll scale down to a 1-week baseline benchmark with synthetic traffic matching your peak concurrency and a representative subset of long tails. We'll aim to capture latency p50/p95, token throughput, and cost estimates using Redwood's runtime.
[01:51] Maya: On evaluation, we will supply 500 labeled transcripts and 200 blind evals for human review. We care about multilingual: English, Spanish, French - roughly 75/15/10 distribution. Some domain-specific legal/terms in English.
[02:10] Priya: Noted. That influences model shortlist - some models handle multilingual better. Jordan, shall we go through the open-model shortlist?
[02:17] Jordan: Yes. Based on initial intake, our recommended shortlist for this POC: Llama-2-13B-instruct (quantized), Mistral-7B-Instruct, Falcon-40B-Open, and MPT-30B or RedPajama-3B? - sorry names, sometimes speech-to-text on the call scrambles. The point is we want a spectrum: 7B-class for cost-efficient, 13B for balanced, and 40B for higher quality where latency allows.
[02:45] Ava: Any thoughts on Llama3 / newer weights? We heard Llama3-70B is better on multilingual.
[02:50] Priya: Llama3-70B would be higher quality but it's heavy for latency/cost. For POC, we usually recommend starting with 13B and a 7B variant - if the 13B doesn't meet quality, we can try 70B in a limited benchmark. Also Mistral has strong multilingual generalization for smaller size.
[03:07] Samir: For latency, our target p95 700ms - do you think 13B quantized on dedicated GPU can hit that?
[03:13] Priya: Yes on dedicated A10/A100-class or optimized runtime with int8 quant; 13B often hits sub-second p95 with batching tuned. For 40B or 70B we'd need more powerful GPU and might hit 700-1200ms depending on sequence length.
[03:27] Leo: Security-wise we need private deployment or dedicated capacity where logs and KV cache are customer-only. Is Redwood Private available for a POC?
[03:34] Jordan: We offer Redwood Dedicated and Private. For POC we can start on Hosted dedicated pool with private namespaces and strict retention, or set up a short-term Private deployment for stricter controls. We'll include both options in the SOW and cost differential.
[03:48] Maya: What about data residency? Some EU customers require EU-based inference. We have EU traffic.
[03:52] Jordan: We have regional routing and can run inference in EU regions. For Private deployments, you can keep everything on-prem/VPC. We'll ask for their residency needs in the security checklist.
[04:02] Priya: Back to benchmarks - we'll run three phases: baseline single-instance latency, scaled concurrency stress test, and qualitative eval on the 200 blind cases. We'll also run ablation for quantization (FP16 vs int8) and a small retrieval-augmented run to see improvement.
[04:20] Ava: On quality tradeoffs, what do you typically see between 7B vs 13B vs 40B?
[04:24] Priya: In our experience: 7B is very cost-efficient but struggles on domain-specific phrasing and low-resource languages; 13B balances general comprehension and cost; 40B/70B gives better contextual understanding and multilingual nuance, especially for low-resource languages, but at higher latency and cost. Retrieval often helps 7B close gaps for domain terms. Also fine-tuning or LoRA helps a lot if you have labeled data.
[04:45] Samir: For the POC we'll likely test the 7B + retrieval and 13B standalone, maybe one 40B run if needed.
[04:52] Jordan: Makes sense. For cost targets - you mentioned 30-40% reduction vs current provider. Can you share rough current numbers?
[04:58] Ava: Right now we're at about $0.12 per 1k tokens effective cost. So target is around $0.07-0.08.
[05:05] Priya: We'll include cost estimates from the benchmark runs; quantization and batching can push cost down. Also Redwood Optimize recommendations may help after POC.
[05:14] Maya: Timeline - we want to ship a decision in 6 weeks. POC length?
[05:18] Jordan: We propose a 6-week POC: week 0 - setup & data ingest, week 1 - baseline benchmarks, week 2 - tuning & runs, week 3 - longer stress and multilingual checks, week 4 - human evals, week 5 - security & integration checks, week 6 - review and decision. We can compress if needed.
[05:34] Ava: That aligns. Who will own infra setup? Samir will handle dataset uploads but Redwood needs to spin up the dedicated test pool.
[05:41] Jordan: Correct - we'll provide access and infra config; Samir will give samples and traffic profiles.
[05:46] Samir: We'll share 500 transcripts + traffic CSV and a subset of 200 blind evals by next Monday.
[05:52] Priya: Great - I'll prepare a benchmark template and a script to replay traffic. We'll also include instructions for tokenization and prompt templates.
[05:59] Leo: A couple of security Qs: 1) Do you support customer-managed KMS for keys? 2) Can we get audit logs for model inputs/outputs reversed? 3) Is there a disable retention mode?
[06:10] Jordan: Yes to KMS - customer-managed KMS/HSM is supported for Private and Dedicated; audit logs available with retention policies; and short retention/disable retention is available in Dedicated/Private. We'll share our security docs.
[06:21] Leo: Also need SAML SSO and RBAC scoped to team and routes.
[06:25] Jordan: Supported - we'll map roles and SSO in the SOW.
[06:28] Maya: On evaluation, we prefer a combined score: 60% human rating, 20% automated similarity, 20% latency/cost composite. Does that make sense?
[06:36] Priya: Yes, that's a clear rubric. We'll implement the scoring harness so results are reproducible.
[06:40] Ava: Any red flags we should consider?
[06:42] Priya: Biggest are: dataset privacy (we addressed with Private/Dedicated), and tail latency during long-context cases; for those we may need KV cache tuning or smaller chunking. Also prompt engineering matters - we'll work with Maya on a prompt suite.
[06:55] Samir: Regarding infra, do you recommend dedicated GPU pools or hosted for latency predictability?
[06:59] Jordan: Dedicated pools give predictable throughput and lower p95 jitter; hosted is simpler but can have variability. For your peaks and SLA needs, Dedicated for POC is recommended. We'll size the pool for expected concurrency and have autoscale for bursts.
[07:12] Maya: Ok. For multilingual, any special preproc?
[07:15] Priya: We'll include language detection step and ensure prompts maintain context. Also include a small transliteration step for certain languages if needed. Retrieval should be language-aware.
[07:25] Leo: On compliance, can you provide SOC2 docs and the ISO portfolio?
[07:28] Jordan: Yes - I'll attach the security pack.
[07:30] Maya: Anything else on models - do you have benchmarking data for Llama-2-13B vs Mistral-7B for Spanish?
[07:36] Priya: We have internal benchmarks - I'll share a summary. Short story: Mistral often does well on Spanish at 7B, but 13B Llama tends to be more consistent across es/fr for summarization tasks. We'll include both in the benchmark matrix.
[07:50] Ava: Perfect. Quick question on integration - we use a serverless front-end that calls your API via a proxy. Any example integration patterns?
[07:57] Jordan: We'll share a quickstart repo with examples for streaming responses, function-calling style JSON outputs, and how to use per-route configs (timeouts, token limits).
[08:06] Samir: For the POC we'll need an API key scoped to test namespace and optionally a temporary cert for VPC peering.
[08:11] Jordan: We'll provision scoped API keys and coordinate VPC peering steps in the security sync.
[08:16] Maya: Great. Let's talk deliverables and due dates quickly.
[08:19] Jordan: Deliverables: POC SOW and pricing (Jordan) - due 2026-05-04. Benchmark template + runner (Priya) - due 2026-05-02. Customer delivers data/traffic (Samir) - due 2026-05-03. Security checklist (Leo) - due 2026-05-05. Baseline benchmark kickoff targeted 2026-05-06.
[08:42] Priya: One more note - for cost calc we'll include quantization and batching scenarios and show per-1k token cost for each model tested.
[08:50] Ava: Good. Any competitive motion to be aware of? We have pilots with Anthropic and OpenAI - want to ensure apples-to-apples comparisons.
[08:57] Jordan: We'll align test harness and prompt sets so results are comparable; include same retrieval context. We'll note differences in model licenses too.
[09:05] Maya: Okay that's it from me.
[09:07] Jordan: Thanks everyone - recap: Jordan sends SOW/pricing and security pack; Priya shares benchmark artifacts; Samir uploads dataset + traffic; Leo shares security checklist; baseline benchmark week of 2026-05-06.
[09:23] Ava: Thanks - looking forward.
[09:26] Jordan: Thanks all, we'll follow up in email with links and the SOW. Bye.

Notes about transcription: occasional mis-heard product names (Llama3 vs llama three), and some timestamps approximate.
